name: illustrator-rotated-sidebar-strip
exporter: Adobe Illustrator 2024 (28.6) - Export As > SVG, Styling: Internal CSS, Object IDs: Layer Names
story: Programme furniture with a vertical strip down the left edge reading bottom-to-top, and a corner clock block the designer scaled to 70% after drawing it full size.
idioms: rotation as a MATRIX with zeros on the diagonal - <text transform="matrix(0 -1 1 0 74 880)"> - because Illustrator never writes rotate()
a SCALED group, transform="matrix(0.7 0 0 0.7 1520 96)", whose children are still drawn at their original size inside it, so a child's own matrix composes with its parent's
the clock's sample written as a clock (21:45), which §3 says may be offered as a countdown rather than assumed to be one
a compound PostScript face name with no space in the family (font-family:'JetBrainsMono-Regular') beside the plain 'Archivo-Bold'
_x20_ escape with data-name holding the original spelling (id="Clock_x20_block" data-name="Clock block")
Generator comment naming the SVG Export Plug-In build, root attrs in Illustrator's order with x="0px" y="0px", viewBox/width/height and xml:space="preserve" on tab-indented continuation lines
style="enable-background:new 0 0 1920 1080;" on <svg> and a <style type="text/css"> block as a direct child, one property per .stN class
unitless letter-spacing in a class, font-size in px in its own class
<rect y="0" ...> with the zero x omitted
tab indentation, one tab per nesting level
whyThisMatters: Every transform in the corpus so far is a translation - matrix(1 0 0 1 tx ty), or Inkscape's translate() on a layer - so the identity part of the matrix has never once been anything but the identity. Here one line is rotated a quarter turn and two more sit inside a 70% group, which is the first time a text's drawn width is not its width on screen and a child's matrix has to compose with its parent's. A field box derived from an unrotated reading of a rotated line lands somewhere the words are not, and a box measured inside a scaled group is 43% too big - both invisible until an operator types, and both entirely ordinary things to draw. Vertical strips and scaled-down furniture are what a results programme is made of.
